Series and parallel combination of resistors
Electromotive force (emf), internal resistance, and cells in combination

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Drifting electrons (I = nAev_d) obey Ohm microscopically (ρ = m/ne²τ) until heat bends the line. Kirchhoff's junction (charge) and loop (energy) laws solve any network; real cells add internal r (V = E − Ir). The Wheatstone bridge weaponises balance: at null deflection no current crosses the middle, so ratios lock — P/Q = R/S — and unknown resistances, meter bridges and potentiometers all reduce to comparing lengths.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: I = nAev_d · V = IR, R = ρL/A (ρ rises with T for metals)  ·  junction ΣI = 0 · loop ΣEMF = ΣIR  ·  Wheatstone: P/Q = R/S at null  ·  meter bridge: R = S·l/(100−l)  ·  potentiometer: E₁/E₂ = l₁/l₂; internal r = R(l₁−l₂)/l₂

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Bridge balance needs the galvanometer at TRUE null (sensitive, tapped not continuously connected). Meter bridge assumes uniform wire (R ∝ length) — file the wire, ruin the ratio. Potentiometer comparison needs the same driver current through the wire for both measurements. Ohm's law needs steady temperature.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Balanced bridge: middle branch removable (no current) — redraw without it. Meter bridge with l = 40 cm against S = 60 Ω: R = 60×40/60 = 40 Ω. Potentiometer measures EMF without drawing current (no r-drop) — voltmeters cannot. Shorted resistor: current takes the zero path entirely.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Meter bridge: unknown R balances standard S at null point l cm from the left: R/S = l/(100−l) → R = S·l/(100−l). Derivation: uniform wire splits resistance ∝ lengths; balance P/Q = R/S with P ∝ l, Q ∝ (100−l). Swap R and S and average to kill end-correction errors.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Bridges measure at balance only — off-null they are ordinary inaccurate networks. Contact and end resistances bias meter bridges (interchange + mean). Potentiometers need longer wires than the EMF under test. Kirchhoff's loop law fails with induced EMF (changing flux).

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Balance: no current in the middle branch → the two left nodes sit at equal potential and so do the right nodes. Left arm ratio P/Q equals right arm R/S because the same node-to-node drops scale identically: V_A − V_C over V_C − V_B is common to both sides → P/Q = R/S. Potentiometer: V ∝ l along a uniform current-carrying wire gives E₁/E₂ = l₁/l₂ directly.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: 'Balanced bridge' → erase the middle branch, recompute series/parallel. Meter bridge: R = S·l/(100−l), then interchange-and-mean. Two-resistor parallel: product/sum. Cells in series aiding/opposing: add/subtract EMFs, add internal r's.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB-style: Wheatstone principle + unknown-resistance numerical; meter-bridge derivation with interchange correction; potentiometer EMF comparison + internal-resistance form; Kirchhoff network solution.
